chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
title: Paramount Theatre with Jacquet's big band, then sailing to Europe without the trio
summary: After Christmas at the Paramount, Sarah, her husband, valet and Malachi sail on the Liberte because the budget cannot carry Crosby and Freeman.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: We finished the tour... I think it started around October, and we finished it around the middle of December, after which we started preparing to go into the Paramount Theatre with Illinois Jacquet's big band, at that time which was a very good band, including people like Budd Johnson and a host of other people that were just excellent musicians. And they had a good show there, too. I think George Kirby was also on that show, and it included this team of Stump and Stumpy. Of course, Sarah Vaughan was the headliner. And through the Christmas holidays we played the Paramount Theatre -- were there for I think two or three weeks.

Right after the closing of the Paramount Theatre job was going to be Sarah's first trip to Europe. And we began making preparations to go to Europe. Everybody was excited, because none of us had been to Europe before. You know, we got passports and stuff like that. At that particular time, air travel to Europe was nothing like it is now. Most people were still using the big boats, like the Queen Mary and the S.S. United States... We went over on the French boat, the Liberte.
But the sad thing about that particular trip was that it was told to Bruz and Israel that they couldn't take them to

Europe, because financially the money wasn't big enough to carry a trio. And I really regretted to have to leave these fellows. But Sarah went to Europe with just her and her husband and the valet -- his name was Johnny Gary, another guy who I really became good friends with. The four of us went. We boarded the Liberte and went to London from New York, which proved to be at that particular time I think about a three-and-a-half-day trip.
